questions.question: In a classroom model of natural selection, students pick up green and white cocktail sticks from a patch of green grass. What does this simple model demonstrate?
options: How different fertilizers affect grass growth
How camouflage affects an organism's chance of being captured
How physical exercise increases muscle mass in animals
How plants compete for sunlight in a dense forest

questions.question: If green and white cocktail sticks are used to model natural selection on a green lawn, the green ones are picked up less. How would the prediction change if the lawn became covered in white frost?
options: Both colors would be picked up at exactly the same rate as before.
Green sticks would now be harder to see and less likely to be picked up.
White sticks would now be harder to see and less likely to be picked up.
All sticks would immediately dissolve in the frost.

questions.question: What is the scientific term for the biological features that make an organism well suited to survive in its specific environment?
options: Adaptations
Lifespans
Acquisitions
Variations

questions.question: Why must individuals of the same or different species compete with each other in an ecosystem?
options: Because ecosystems have unlimited space and energy
Because resources like food, water, and shelter are limited
Because predators always share their food voluntarily
Because organisms choose to compete to gain new genes

questions.question: How does variation within a species affect the outcome of competition for limited resources?
options: It ensures that all individuals survive and reproduce equally.
It means some individuals are better adapted and will compete more successfully.
It causes all individuals to suddenly change their DNA during their lifetime.
It stops competition completely by creating different niches for every single individual.

questions.question: What is the definition of a scientific theory, such as the theory of evolution by natural selection?
options: A temporary guess made by a single scientist without any data
A general explanation, developed from evidence, that explains many different examples
A set of laws that cannot be modified or updated under any circumstances
An untested idea that only applies to a single specific organism

questions.question: Which of the following statements is true regarding how new advantageous features arise in a population?
options: They are planned in advance by organisms to prepare for future climates.
They appear randomly and are maintained over generations by natural selection.
They are actively created by an animal's desire to change its body shape.
They only appear when an organism decides to move to a new habitat.

questions.question: An individual dog exercises heavily and develops very strong muscles during its lifetime. Why is this change not considered evolution?
options: Because evolution only occurs in plants, not in animals.
Because changes in the features of an individual within its lifetime are not evolution.
Because muscle growth is not an advantageous feature for survival.
Because the dog did not change its diet to match its new muscles.

questions.question: What exactly are all fossils?
options: Preserved tissue that has remained completely soft and unchanged
Rocks that have been carved by ancient humans to look like animals
The mineralised remains of once-living organisms or of traces left behind by organisms
Living organisms that have hibernated underground for millions of years

questions.question: When scientists study fossils to understand the history of life, what must they keep in mind?
options: There are limitations to the conclusions and explanations that can be made from fossil evidence.
Fossils are 100% complete and always show every soft tissue of every creature that ever lived.
Fossils can only be found in areas where active volcanoes are currently erupting.
Fossils only preserve organisms that died less than one hundred years ago.

questions.question: A tree loses a branch in a severe storm, leaving a scar. Why will its offspring, grown from its seeds, not have this same scar?
options: Because the scar is genetic variation, which is never passed on.
Because environmental variation is not heritable and cannot be passed on.
Because seeds are only produced by trees that have never been damaged.
Because scars are repaired by natural selection before the seeds can form

questions.question: Which type of variation can be passed on from parents to their offspring?
options: Variation caused by physical injuries during life
Variation caused by learning a new trick or behavior
Genetic variation, which is heritable
Environmental variation caused by sun exposure

questions.question: In a population, what is the consequence of certain individuals being better adapted to their environment?
options: They are more likely to migrate to another planet.
They are more likely to pass on heritable, advantageous features to their offspring.
They will stop reproducing to allow less-adapted individuals to catch up.
They lose their genetic variation and become identical to other species.

questions.question: Based on scientific evidence, approximately how long ago was the Earth formed?
options: 4.5 million years ago
4.5 billion years ago
350 thousand years ago
500 million years ago

questions.question: According to fossil evidence, what is the approximate age range of the oldest and newest fossils found?
options: Oldest are 10 thousand years old; newest are 100 years old
Oldest are 3.5 billion years old; newest are around 10 thousand years old
Oldest are 500 million years old; newest are 200 million years old
Oldest are 4.5 billion years old; newest are 3.8 billion years old

questions.question: Which of the following correctly matches the estimated appearance of groups of organisms according to scientific evidence?
options: Land plants 200mya, mammals 500mya, modern humans 10 thousand years ago
Land plants 500mya, mammals 200mya, modern humans 350k years ago
Land plants 3.8 billion years ago, mammals 3.5 billion years ago, modern humans 500mya
Land plants 350k years ago, mammals 200mya, modern humans 10 thousand years ago

questions.question: How do scientists divide the vast history of the Earth to make it easier to study and understand?
options: Into weeks, months, and decades
Into eons, periods, and epochs
Into lightyears, parsecs, and miles
Into ancient, middle, and modern days of the week
